verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents real containment primitives — a sandbox backend for tool execution, hardened-container 'cells' for multi-tenant isolation, SecretRef-based credential handling, and a `security audit` drift-check command — which on paper map well to the sandboxing/policy/permission story. However, hands-on community reports directly contradict the effectiveness of this model: one commenter states 'the openclaw security model is the equivalent of running as root - i.e. full access,' and a comparison to nanoclaw notes OpenClaw lacks the containerized filesystem isolation that a more secure alternative provides, plus a reported incident where a top community skill was actually a malware installer. missing for 10: independent verification that sandbox mode is enabled/enforced by default, third-party audit of the sandboxing backend's actual blast-radius reduction, and resolution of the 'root-equivalent access' criticism.
